<assessment>SOURCE shows a tall gridded tower stepping down toward a planted low wing, recessed glazed and outdoor bays, a darker lower facade zone, transparent street frontage, and a neighboring punched-window building with a vegetated end wall. CURRENT captures these broad relationships and now demonstrates projecting grid members, glazing reveals, terrace guards and vegetation relief. Remaining differences concern the full-bay recesses, low-wing terrace articulation and neighboring window rhythm. SOURCE provides one street perspective: rear elevations, concealed connections and exact dimensions remain unverified. No definite slab penetration, floating guard or plant/building collision is established by these captures.</assessment>
<issue priority="1" view="front">
problem: SOURCE has substantial recessed outdoor bays within the tower grid, particularly on its right-facing elevation. CURRENT represents several of these as short dark slots within otherwise continuous glazed bays; the close inspection establishes window reveals but does not establish equivalent outdoor-bay depth.
action: Locally open and deepen the corresponding source-visible bays, providing connected floors, side returns, recessed glazing and perimeter guards. Preserve the demonstrated grid relief and darker lower facade treatment.
</issue>
<issue priority="2" view="roof">
problem: SOURCE shows layered planted outdoor pockets above the low wing and along the setbacks. CURRENT has terrace surfaces and guards, but the connector remains predominantly a broad flat surface with isolated, regularly spaced planting boxes, losing the source-visible planted-edge depth and layering.
action: Adjust the existing low-wing terrace edges and planting zones to form the observed stepped outdoor pockets. Connect their surfaces and perimeter assemblies without extending slabs through adjoining enclosure.
</issue>
<issue priority="3" view="front">
problem: The neighboring facade remains too densely subdivided: CURRENT uses repeated shallow upper window rows and narrow lower openings, while SOURCE shows a less compressed rhythm of punched openings. The previously missing vegetated end-wall relief is now present.
action: Locally revise the source-visible window spacing, proportions and upper-row arrangement. Preserve the neighbor's adjacency, dark ground-floor openings and established vegetation relief.
</issue>
<keep>
Pale projecting grid members and visible glazing reveals demonstrated in the close inspection.
Distinct darker lower facade zone.
Neighboring building's dark ground-floor openings.
Vegetation relief on the neighboring far-right end wall.
</keep>
